subject: Clarify: erase notification obligations vs backup access carve-outs
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda.park@skyline-fintech.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@skyline-fintech.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: erase notification obligations vs backup access carve-outs

David —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security and legal teams on the DPA redlines: they want explicit language about what constitutes an "erase" vs a retained backup snapshot. Specific asks below — can you confirm Redwood's current behavior and suggest contract wording we can accept?

1) Certified erasure: we need a clause that Redwood will provide a time-stamped certificate or manifest for customer-requested erasures that includes which data stores were targeted (primary, replica, backup snapshots) and the retention windows applied. Is that something you can provide?

2) Backups: Skyline requires backups to be retained for 90 days for operational recovery, but those backups must be excluded from the customer's erase request unless otherwise agreed. We need clear carve-out language and an SLA for how quickly backups are purged after the 90-day mark.

3) Notification: if Redwood must retain subsets of data in backups for legal/regulatory reasons, we need a prior-notice obligation and an estimated timeframe. Also, what is Redwood's process for notifying customers when a recovery from backups may reintroduce deleted data?

4) Key rotation / BYOK implications: if we rotate keys or rekey, does that change your ability to produce an erase manifest for encrypted backups?

Attached: our suggested redline language (redline-proposal-dpaclause.docx).

Can we get Redwood's proposed contract wording and an operational playbook (even a high-level erase manifest template) by end of week? Our procurement wants to close the SOW next week.

Thanks,
Linda Park
Head of Security Programs
Skyline Fintech

From: david.kim@redwood.ai <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Park <linda.park@skyline-fintech.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: erase notification obligations vs backup access carve-outs

Hi Linda —

Really helpful list, thank you. Short answers up-front and then I'll loop in Karthik/Laura/Jonas for the redline language and playbook.

1) Certified erasure: Yes, we can provide a timestamped "erase manifest" that lists logical datasets, S3 prefixes, and which serving replicas were targeted. It will include a signed hash and operator id. Operationally, we currently scrub data from live shards and issue the manifest within 48 hours; backups are handled separately (see below).

2) Backups: We generally treat backups as a separate retention tier. If you request immediate erasure of all copies, we can offer an on-demand backup purge at contract cost, but the standard workflow is a timed purge (e.g., 90 days) plus an option for expedited removal as an add-on. We should capture that as: "Backups and archival snapshots are excluded from on-demand erasure requests unless the parties agree to an expedited purge fee and schedule."

3) Notification: We can commit to notify customers within 72 hours if a legal/regulatory hold prevents timely purge of backups, with an estimated hold duration and the authority invoking the hold. Regarding reintroduction from recovery: our restore playbook includes a pre-restore scan and scrub step; we will notify the customer before any restore that could reintroduce deleted identifiers.

4) BYOK: If keys are customer-managed and backups encrypted with BYOK, Redwood can produce a manifest of which objects are encrypted and their KMS key ids, but we cannot perform an operator-side crypto wipe without key access. If keys are rotated, we record rotation events in the manifest.

I'll have Karthik draft a redline that captures the above and attach an operational erase manifest template.

-David

--
David Kim
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify: erase notification obligations vs backup access carve-outs

Team —

Draft redline language below (high level). Attaching the erase-playbook-v1.pdf to show operational steps. Please review and call out any holes.

DRAFT CONTRACT LANGUAGE (proposed)
1. Definitions: "Erase" means deletion of Customer Data from primary production storage and replicas used for live serving. "Backup Snapshots" means point-in-time copies used for disaster recovery, archival, or long-term retention.

2. Backup Carve-Out: Unless otherwise agreed in writing, Backup Snapshots are excluded from "Erase" requests for a period of ninety (90) days following their creation. Customer may request expedited purge of Backup Snapshots; Redwood will perform expedited purge subject to an agreed fee and schedule.

3. Erase Manifest: Upon completion of an Erase request of production and replica storage, Redwood shall provide a signed Erase Manifest within forty-eight (48) hours that includes: (a) unique manifest id; (b) timestamp of completion; (c) list of logical storage locations removed (prefixes/buckets/ids); (d) operator id and job id; (e) hash digest of manifest; (f) note on whether backup snapshots were targeted or excluded.

4. Notification & Holds: If Redwood receives a request or order that prevents timely deletion (e.g., lawful hold), Redwood will notify Customer within seventy-two (72) hours of the reason and expected duration, and will provide periodic updates not less than every thirty (30) days.

5. BYOK and Crypto Observability: If Customer provides encryption keys (BYOK), Redwood will include key identifiers and rotation timestamps in the Erase Manifest. Where Customer retains exclusive control of keys, Redwood's ability to perform crypto-scrub operations on encrypted backups is dependent on Customer providing necessary key materials or instructions.

6. Recovery/Restore Safeguards: Prior to any restore that may reintroduce deleted data into production, Redwood will: (a) notify Customer at least five (5) business days in advance; (b) run an automated scan to flag potential reintroduced identifiers; and (c) only proceed with restore subject to Customer written approval or a documented exception process.

Please flag any legalese Laura thinks is problematic. I tried to balance operational guarantees with realistic constraints.

-Karthik

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, Linda Park <linda.park@skyline-fintech.com>, legal@skyline-fintech.com
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: erase notification obligations vs backup access carve-outs

Thanks Karthik — this is a good operational-first draft. A couple of legal notes to propose for the redline (we'll send a tracked version to Linda):

- Change "within forty-eight (48) hours" for Erase Manifest to "within five (5) business days" to allow for verification and chain-of-custody logging.
- Add explicit statement that manifests are evidence of operator actions but do not constitute a warranty about third-party backups outside Redwood control (e.g., customer-managed offsite copies).
- For Backup Carve-Out: add a clause that Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to purge backups earlier than 90 days if requested and lawful.
- For Notification & Holds: define "legal/regulatory hold" and require Redwood to provide the name of the authority and redacted copy of the request where permitted.

I recommend we attach erase-playbook-v1.pdf as an operational appendix and provide a one-page matrix in the DPA summarizing tiers (live, replica, short-term backup, long-term archive) and typical timelines.

Laura
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

Linda —

Thanks again. Attached is the erase-playbook-v1.pdf and our proposed tracked redline (redline-proposal-dpaclause.docx). High-level changes from your draft: 

- We propose the Erase Manifest delivery window as five (5) business days (see Laura note) with a commitment to initial acknowledgement within 48 hours.
- Backup carve-out language retained with a commercial-efforts clause for earlier purge and an expedited purge offer (fee-based).
- We'll include key identifier metadata for BYOK customers; expedited crypto-scrub requires key material or an agreed process.
- Notification for holds: we will notify within 72 hours and provide redacted authority documents where permitted.

Next steps: if Skyline legal can confirm acceptance of the five-business-day manifest window and the backup carve-out + expedited purge option, we can move this clause into the DPA and attach erase-playbook-v1 as an appendix. If preferred, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the playbook.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — hoping to close the SOW this week.

Best,
David
